clue.text: Unwillingly allow, say, in C Dickens book

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for say sits inside the title letters

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Charles Dickens novel
say introduces an example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly permits something, as described in a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'C Dickens book' points to Barnaby Rudge, shortened here to its initial plus surname; the example abbreviation is tucked between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to grant or permit something only reluctantly.

clue.text: Rainforest-dwellers in S American region -one's at the top

indicators.note: at the top asks for the letter for one to be shifted to the front of the region's name

parts.note: the Guianas are a region of northern South America
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Animals living in South American rainforest, with one perched at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: In GUIANAS the I moves from third place to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanas are lizards found in tropical forests of the Americas, so they are forest inhabitants.

clue.text: One of many regiments in Irish police

explanation.surface: A regiment among many serving in the Irish police force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish police are the Garda Síochána, literally 'Guardians', and a garda is commonly called a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guards are a set of British army regiments; the Irish police force are informally called the guards.

clue.text: Pettifogger taped broadcast about Norway

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the country's abbreviation
broadcast suggests scattering, so the letters of taped are rearranged

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A nit-picker's recording is aired on a programme about Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns TAPED into PEDAT, and 'about' wraps it around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A pettifogger quibbles over trivial details, just as a nit-picking stickler does.

clue.text: If nothing else, finally conquered summit of Everest

indicators.note: conquered pictures the outer phrase capturing and holding the peak's letter

parts.note: finally means at last

indicators.note: summit of picks the top, or first, letter of Everest

explanation.surface: A climber at last tops Everest, if nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the first letter of Everest, goes inside AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: At least is an idiom meaning as a minimum or at any rate.

clue.text: A sucker for credit

explanation.surface: Looking for someone foolish enough to lend money.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a bloodsucking parasite; on tick is British slang for buying on credit.

clue.text: Troon spoon?

explanation.surface: A rhyming pair of words with a question mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Troon is a famous Scottish golf course and its club; a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Troon is a golfing association on the Ayrshire coast; a spoon is an implement for hitting a golf ball.

clue.text: Idiot has approved first lady witness

indicators.note: has means the fool's word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a loon is a foolish person
OK means approved
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen, the first lady of the land

explanation.surface: A fool gets endorsement from the first lady as a witness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' looks like a president's wife, but crosswords use it for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A looker-on is a spectator or observer of an event.

clue.text: Long for Bay Watch at heart

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

indicators.note: at heart picks the central letter of watch

explanation.surface: Wishing for the TV show Baywatch, deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the middle letter of WATCH. The surface evokes the TV show Baywatch.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to desire or crave something, especially another's.

clue.text: In Paris agreement I put forward promise

indicators.note: put forward asks for the letter I to be moved to the front

parts.note: oui is French for yes

explanation.surface: In Paris a deal is struck and I make a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: OUI with its I brought to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An IOU is a written pledge to repay a debt.

clue.text: Natural Icelandic part of this family? No

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is native Icelandic a member of this language family? No.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters run from natURAL into ICelandic. Icelandic is Germanic, not in the Uralic family, hence 'No'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uralic is the language family including Finnish and Hungarian, which Icelandic does not belong to.

clue.text: Andy's beginning with love-15 — changing juice

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of Andy's
changing tells us to rearrange the letters of love and the cross-referenced word

parts.note: taken as written
15 refers to the answer at 15-down, a long period of years

explanation.surface: Andy Murray starts a tennis game at love-fifteen, then switches drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes LOEVERA. The tennis score love-15 is misdirection: 15 is a cross-reference to 15-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is a plant whose gel or sap is used as a soothing juice.

clue.text: It's swept twice a day by 26 25 and put back

definitions.text: It's swept twice a day by 26 25

indicators.note: back tells us the synonym of put is read in reverse

parts.note: put, as in laid down, means laid

explanation.surface: Something the hour hand sweeps across twice daily, and replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 25 is the linked answer, the clock's shorter pointer, which circles the clock face twice a day.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock dial is the face whose circle the short pointer travels round every twelve hours.

clue.text: Looks over occasional titles and papers

indicators.note: over pictures the stares covering the selected letters

parts.note: gazes means looks steadily

indicators.note: occasional picks every other letter of titles

explanation.surface: Someone skims the odd headline in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasional' takes T, T, E from TITLES; GAZES goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazettes are newspapers or official journals.

clue.text: Long period of years essentially wasted

indicators.note: wasted suggests ruined, so those letters are rearranged
essentially picks the core letters of years, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: Many years of one's life have essentially been squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' gives EAR from YEARS, which 'wasted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a lengthy span of history.

clue.text: Occasional faulty radio's carried by special constable

indicators.note: carried by means the rearranged letters are held inside the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: SPC is an abbreviation for special police constable

indicators.note: faulty tells us the letters of radio are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman's broken radio works only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' gives ORADI, which sits between the second and third letters of the officer's abbreviation. The possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means happening at irregular intervals, now and then.

clue.text: Secret police turn over suspect tapes

indicators.note: over means the word for turn is laid over and around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a go is a turn

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful, so the letters of tapes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Security services hand over dubious recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' gives ESTAP; 'turn over' looks like a reversal instruction, but turn is a synonym and over the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was Nazi Germany's feared state security force.

clue.text: Racetrack taken over as an afterthought?

indicators.note: taken over tells us the letters are turned round

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A racing circuit is acquired almost as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: A and PS reversed. Spa-Francorchamps is the Belgian Grand Prix circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spa is the famous motor-racing circuit in the Belgian Ardennes.

clue.text: Blimey! Gentleman's captured a pirate!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey

indicators.note: captured means the title holds the letter A inside it

parts.note: sir is the form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: An excited cry that a gentleman has caught a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blimey' and 'cor' are both British exclamations of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a pirate, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Sub's almost upright

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: standing means upright, on one's feet

explanation.surface: A substitute is very nearly vertical.
explanation.walkthrough: STANDING loses its last letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute who takes someone's place.

clue.text: Schooner maybe a girl served up in hostelry

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the inn

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry

indicators.note: served up, in a down clue, means the letters are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl brings a schooner of sherry up in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' gives DIAMA. A schooner is also a large glass of sherry or beer, the sense the pub surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a sailing ship trading with India, so a schooner could be an example of a vessel.

clue.text: What mules do, running round horse?

definitions.text: What mules do, running round horse?

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters surround the horse
running suggests movement and disorder, so the letters of mules are rearranged

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: Drug couriers bustle around a horse with contraband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' gives SMULE. Mules here are drug couriers, not the animals, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are people who carry illegal goods past customs, i.e. they move contraband secretly.

clue.text: A smart order among Piazza Italia's starters?

definitions.text: A smart order among Piazza Italia's starters?

indicators.note: among places the rearranged letters between the two initials
starters picks the first letters of Piazza and Italia's
order means the letters of a smart are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A chic dish to request among the first courses at an Italian square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges A SMART to ASTRAM, set between P and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is smoked spiced beef, a stylish thing to request at a deli.

clue.text: Disputed region in New Jersey area protected by bar

indicators.note: protected by means the inner letters are sheltered inside the bar

parts.note: a pub is a bar
NJ is the US state abbreviation for New Jersey

explanation.surface: A contested territory in New Jersey is guarded by a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Punjab was split between India and Pakistan at partition in 1947, hence 'Disputed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjab is a territory divided and contested between India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Rely on promoting son as powerful member

indicators.note: promoting, in a down clue, sends the letter for son higher up, to the top

parts.note: to trust is to rely on

explanation.surface: Depending on a son being moved up as an influential figure.
explanation.walkthrough: In TRUST the second S moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a strong structural bar, a load-bearing element in a frame.

clue.text: See 26
Pointer dog runs across archway now and then

indicators.note: runs across means the dog's letters stretch across, enclosing the others

parts.note: a hound is a dog

indicators.note: now and then picks every other letter of archway

explanation.surface: A pointer dog dashes across an archway from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now and then' takes R, H, A from ARCHWAY, placed inside HOUND. 'Pointer' and 'dog' lure you towards the breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour hand is the shorter pointer on a clock face.

clue.text: Time Team's coming, say, beneath you?

indicators.note: say indicates what follows is spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.note: Time Team was a British TV archaeology show, so its crew would be in for a dig

explanation.surface: The TV archaeologists are arriving: would that be beneath you?
explanation.walkthrough: Time Team was a British TV series in which archaeologists excavated a site in three days; 'in for a dig' said quickly gives the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig, short for Latin infra dignitatem, means undignified, below one's status.

clue.text: Pity he defended director in row

indicators.note: in places the pronoun and abbreviation inside the rowing word

parts.note: to row you use an oar

indicators.note: defended pictures the pronoun guarding the director's letter by surrounding it

explanation.surface: Regret that a man stood up for a director during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defended' gives HDE. 'Pity' looks like a noun or verb, but it is the exclamation; 'row' means a quarrel on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Oh dear is an exclamation of sympathy or dismay, like what a shame.

clue.text: Ungulate tosses its head back

indicators.note: its head is the opening three letters of the word, and tossing them back reads them in reverse

parts.note: the leading three letters of ungulate

explanation.surface: A hoofed animal throws its head back.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three letters of UNGULATE, read backwards. A gnu is itself an ungulate.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is an African antelope, a hoofed mammal.

clue.text: In navy, a tunic gets creased on admiral's shoulders

indicators.note: creased suggests crumpled cloth, so the letters of a tunic are rearranged
shoulders are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of admiral

explanation.surface: In the fleet, a uniform jacket is crumpled across the admiral's shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creased' turns A TUNIC into NAUTIC, then AL, the first and last letters of ADMIRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to ships, sailors and the navy.

clue.text: Strip absconder America expelled

indicators.note: expelled means the letter for America is thrown out

parts.note: a runaway is someone who absconds

explanation.surface: A fugitive is thrown out of America.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNAWAY loses its second A.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is a landing strip for aircraft.
